notes: Research draft, not wired into the app. Sources inherited from the recommendation and first-government research retain their original access dates; newly retrieved sources were read on 2026-11-05.

The term window runs from this election to the next Knesset election. Government tenure may extend past that window. Mid-term institutional succession is recorded in formation.events; it is not a new post-election recommendation round.

Additional dated mid-term acts that do not fit the proposal’s closed formation type vocabulary are kept as formalStep=true entries in government.changes (Dated-compatible). No new formation enum values are introduced.

cites.quote: 'I arrived at the conclusion that Mr. Menachem Begin has more chances than any other candidate to form the next government -- that is, 61 Knesset members spoke out in favor of his forming the government.
Begin has support in principle from three religious parties -- the National Religious Party, the Tami Party and the Agudat Israel Party -- which hold a total of 13 seats in the Knesset (parliament).
Aharon Abu Hatzeira's Tami faction, with three seats, indicated to Navon that it preferred a government headed by Begin, while Moshe Dayan's two-seat Telem party leaned toward Labor
ב-10 ביולי זימן נבון את סיעות הבית להתייעצויות ב-13 וב-14 ביולי

notes: Partial: President Navon stated that 61 MKs backed Begin (Likud 48 + NRP 6 + Agudat Yisrael 4 + Tami 3, the parties UPI names). What the Alignment, Hadash, Tehiya, Telem, Shinui and Ratz told the President is not stated as a recommendation in the sources retrieved (JTA describes leanings only), so they are 'not stated', not 'no recommendation'.

Mandate given to Begin on 15 July 1981 (Navon's letter is dated 16 July in the State Archives account). UPI's 1981 pages returned 403 to a direct request on 2026-11-05; their quotes are from a search-index extract. The State Archives chapter also returned 403; its quote is from a search-index extract.

events.textEn: President Navon consulted the factions on 13–14 July.

cites.quote: formally summoned by President Yitzhak Navon today to form a new government

values.value: 15 July 1981 in the existing JTA/UPI research
16 July 1981 presidential letter in the State Archives account

conflicts.resolution: Use 15 July for the tasking per the existing contemporary JTA/UPI research. The JTA bulletin dated 16 July reports the preceding day’s event; the State Archives dates the presidential letter to 16 July. The letter scan has not been inspected.

term.inclusionRule: At least two independently authored qualifying chronologies, including one official or academic, plus direct support for the date. The Knesset and MFA histories count separately; the JVL mirror is not another independent source. Formal government succession steps are recorded separately in formation.events.

events.textEn: Israel completed its withdrawal from the Sinai Peninsula under the peace treaty with Egypt.
events.textHe: ישראל השלימה את נסיגתה מחצי האי סיני במסגרת הסכם השלום עם מצרים.

cites.quote: the withdrawal from the Sinai was completed with the evacuation of Yamit
Israel’s three-stage withdrawal from Sinai Peninsula completed

events.textEn: The First Lebanon War began (Operation Peace for Galilee).

candidatesPending.label: Sabra and Shatila massacre and Kahan inquiry
candidatesPending.why: Both Knesset history and MFA timeline select the massacre and inquiry. The candidate bundles September 1982 killings with the 1983 report. Knesset history also misdates appointment of the inquiry to November 1982. Split the acts and inspect direct dates before promotion.

candidatesPending.label: Bus 300 affair
candidatesPending.why: Both Knesset history and MFA timeline select the 1984 bus affair/hijacking. The candidate needs to distinguish the hijacking from the later killing/disclosure acts and verify their direct dates.

endedBy.textEn: The Knesset enacted a dissolution law; the next election was held on 23 July 1984.
